examples: I was walking home.
She was walking home.
You were walking home.
They were walking home.
I was not walking home.
I wasn't walking home.
They were not walking home.
They weren't walking home.
Was she walking?
Were they walking?
Negative-Interrogative: Wasn't I helping? Weren't you helping?

items.case: for an action that was in the middle of happening at a stated time in the past
examples: At 8 o'clock last night she was watching TV.
He was playing tennis at 4:30 pm yesterday.
He was studying for his Maths test at 9 o'clock last night.

items.case: for two or more actions which were happening at the same time in the past (simultaneous actions)
examples: At 5 o'clock yesterday afternoon Ben was doing his homework while his dad was cooking dinner.
Mum was reading a book while Dad was watching TV.
While I was sunbathing, Tim was swimming.

items.case: for a past action which was in progress when another action interrupted it
examples: Linda was watching TV when the phone rang.
While I was getting dressed the bell rang.
Kate was sunbathing when it started to rain.
items.hint: The longer action is in the Past Continuous, the shorter action is in the Past Simple.

items.case: to describe the background to the events in a story
examples: We were walking in the woods. It was raining hard ...
She was flying to Paris. The sun was shining...

cards.title: Was / Were going to
cards.subtitle: plans in the past that did not happen

items: Was going to is used to express fixed arrangements in the past, unfulfilled plans or an action which someone intended to do in the past but didn't do.

examples: He got up early. He was going to catch the 6 o'clock train.
She was going to travel around Europe but she didn't because she fell ill.

items.case: intention that was not carried out
examples: She was going to buy a new car but in the end she repaired her old one.
items.hint: She intended to buy a car but she didn't.
